origin: A complete real sub-agent transcript, 14 lines. Redacted by field allowlist; the skill and sub-agent-type labels are kept verbatim because they are closed-vocabulary categories, never prompt or file content.
method: Counted from the raw JSONL by a second implementation written against the log's shape, never calling internal/parser. The first adjudication of this trace read a response's usage off its first block line, which understates output; the parser was right.

derivations.records: 7 assistant lines carry 4 distinct message.id values.
derivations.input_tokens: sum of input_tokens over the 4 distinct ids, taken once per id.
derivations.output_tokens: 1,989: the largest output_tokens each of the 4 ids reports. A response's block lines each repeat its usage, but the count only reaches its true total on the last block -- an earlier block reports what had been emitted when it was written. Taking the first line's figure gives 50 here, and this trace is where that rule became visible: the other two Claude traces happen to carry the final count on their first block, so they cannot tell the two readings apart. It is also why the restate path maximises a token count rather than assigning it -- a session read mid-response would otherwise be pinned at the partial number.
derivations.cache_read_tokens: sum of cache_read_input_tokens over the 4 ids.
derivations.cache_write_tokens: sum of cache_creation_input_tokens over the 4 ids.
derivations.cache_write_1h_tokens: usage.cache_creation reports the whole write as the 5-minute tier on every turn here, so the 1-hour portion is zero -- a measured zero, unlike the absent field a source that publishes no split would leave.
derivations.reasoning_tokens: Claude Code publishes no thinking count.
derivations.lines_added: no toolUseResult in this transcript describes a file change.
derivations.rework_lines: no line activity, so nothing to undo.
derivations.edits: none of the 4 tool_use blocks names an edit tool.
derivations.tool_calls: 4 tool_use blocks across the 7 assistant lines.
derivations.tool_errors: one tool_result block flagged is_error, on a line carrying no denial -- so it is the tool failing rather than a human refusing, and it belongs to the turn that made the call rather than to the line reporting it.
derivations.compactions: no compaction boundary in this transcript.
derivations.skipped: every line is valid JSON and every assistant line carries a message.id.
derivations.attribution: every assistant line carries attributionSkill 'deep-research' and attributionAgent 'workflow-subagent', so all 4 records' tokens are attributable to both dimensions -- which is what ai.skill.tokens and ai.agent.tokens are summed from. One turn also carries diagnostics.cache_miss_reason 'tools_changed', the vendor's own reason its prompt could not be served from cache.
derivations.steps: 8: one step per distinct assistant response (4) plus one per tool_use block (4).
derivations.step_outcomes: 0. This capture predates the sequence reading, and its allowlist copied only what the parser read at the time: no tool_use carries an id, so no tool_result can be matched to the call it answers, and every assistant stop_reason is absent. The later sequence.jsonl trace is the one that pins an outcome.
derivations.step_targets: 0. Same reason: no tool_use block carries an input, so no call in this trace names a file. The edit result's own filePath is deliberately not read for a target -- see sequence.jsonl.
